adjudicated.jp: 新川豊は元気だった。いつもだいたい。
adjudicated.en: Shinkawa Yutaka was in high spirits. Almost always.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: レスポンスが早い。
adjudicated.en: Replies came quick.
comments: This sounds like a problem in Gunjou. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 話していてキレが良かった。
adjudicated.en: The way he talked was sharp and clever.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ノリも良かった。
adjudicated.en: Quite good on the back-and-forth of jokes, too.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: その新川が、ある時こんなことを言った。
adjudicated.en: Shinkawa once said this:
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 『姪がさー、やっぱ群青行くんだけどさ、いろいろ教えてやらんと』
adjudicated.en: Shinkawa: 『Got a niece, ya know, 'course she goes to Gunjou, ya know, so she's telling me lots and lots of stuff.』
comments: PCP CCA0018B
adjudicated.assessment: Shinkawa says his niece will also attend Gunjō and that he needs to teach her various things. The English says she already attends and reverses the teaching direction so that she tells him things.

highlights.text: Shinkawa: 『Got a niece, ya know, 'course she goes to Gunjou, ya know, so she's telling me lots and lots of stuff.』

adjudicated.jp: 揉めた。
adjudicated.en: We discussed it harshly.
comments: 揉 used only literally. Wait, no, only laterally. Wait, no, uhmmm -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: しかも相当に可愛いとのこと。
adjudicated.en: How she was fairly cute, for starters.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese adds that she is reportedly quite cute. The English is an ungoverned 'how' fragment and makes the statement the first item in an unstated list.

highlights.text: How she was fairly cute, for starters.

adjudicated.jp: さらに揉めた。羨望と嫉妬だった。
adjudicated.en: And we furthermore discussed. It was envy with jealousy.
comments: See CCA0018B, it's just more remembering of how he didn't exactly look at girls with pure eyes... possibly ever. Not that Taichi isn't being a hypocrite here, but his fears that Yutaka would do bad stuff to Kiri are the source of his jealousy. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says the dispute or agitation intensified because of envy and jealousy. The English reduces it to further discussion and joins the two emotions with the wrong preposition.

highlights.text: we furthermore discussed. It was envy with jealousy.

adjudicated.jp: この二つが揃えば、だいたいどんな相手でも憎める。人間は。
adjudicated.en: If both of those are present, hatred would normally ensue, and regardless of who's their target. It's human.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 俺は憎みはしなかった。
adjudicated.en: I did not have hatred.
comments: See CCC3026, CCC3030 -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says Taichi did not hate him. The English nominalizes the feeling and omits its object.

adjudicated.jp: 続く豊の発言が、よりさらなる衝撃を引き起こしたからだ。
adjudicated.en: But the next remark by Yutaka provoked even further jolts in me:
comments: It's just "I received a shock" written high... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 『本気で、妹みたいなもんなんだよ。同居してるし』
adjudicated.en: Shinkawa: 『Seriously, she's kinda like a little sister, 's all. 's just cohabitation.』
comments: PCP CCA0018B
adjudicated.assessment: Shinkawa says the niece is like a little sister because they live together. The English adds a separate fragment dismissing the situation as 'just cohabitation.'

adjudicated.jp: 可愛い血の繋がらない妹的存在と暮らしている。
adjudicated.en: He is living together with a Cute Non-Blood Related Imouto-like being.
comments: Fetishist term -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese describes living with a cute, unrelated, little-sister-like figure. The English leaves imouto untranslated, capitalizes the entire description, and dehumanizes her as a 'being.'

adjudicated.jp: しかも後に聞いたところでは、両親はほとんど家に帰らないらしい。
adjudicated.en: And also, some time later I heard that their parents seemed to almost never be home.
comments: The typical VN trope of absent parentage (see Misato and Taichi, for starters). It's all but a recipe for your typical nukige, and Yutaka's backstory is that of Rapist Protagonist already. It's very possible that Taichi, at this point, genuinely fears for whoever the cousin is, even if he doesn't recognize Yutaka consciously at this point. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: こういうシチュを、逸般的に同棲と言います。
adjudicated.en: The abovementioned 'chewation is ungenerally referred to as 'sharing the house'.
comments: The opposite of 一般的 (and still pronounced 'ippanteki'), see below -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese makes a visible pun on the ordinary word for 'generally' while calling the situation cohabitation. The English coins an opaque 'chewation,' uses 'ungenerally,' and then downgrades cohabitation to merely sharing a house.

highlights.text: The abovementioned 'chewation is ungenerally referred to as 'sharing the house'.

adjudicated.jp: 二人とも群青に通うことになる。
adjudicated.en: The two of them ended up both going to Gunjou.
adjudicated.assessment: The place name 群青 is Gunjō in standard Hepburn, not 'Gunjou.'

adjudicated.jp: 『おー、姪のことも紹介してやるよ』
adjudicated.en: Shinkawa: 『Oh, I'll be introducing you to the niece then!』
comments: PCP CCA0018B
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 『……たいしたもんじゃないんだけどな……あんま期待すんなよ？』
adjudicated.en: Shinkawa: 『...it ain't much of a big deal so... don't expect much, will ya?』
comments: PCP CCA0018B
adjudicated.assessment: Shinkawa says that his niece is nothing special. The English substitutes an impersonal 'it' and describes a situation as no big deal.

highlights.text: it ain't much of a big deal

adjudicated.jp: たいしたものじゃない。
adjudicated.en: Not much of a big deal.
comments: CP CCA0018B
adjudicated.assessment: The narration repeats that she is supposedly nothing special. The English again turns the person into an unspecified situation.

highlights.text: Not much of a big deal.

adjudicated.jp: 後に俺は、実際に彼女と会うことになった。
adjudicated.en: Later on, I ended up meeting her for real.
comments: Taichi met Kiri before the scene in CCA0018B, but was only properly introduced here. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「じゃ紹介すると、こいつが佐倉霧。家族みたいなモン」
adjudicated.en: Shinkawa: "Introductions then, this here's Sakura Kiri. She's sorta like family."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 一般的にこれを青天の霹靂と言います。
adjudicated.en: The abovementioned is generally referred to as a 'thunderbolt out of the blue'.
comments: Opposite of that 'ungenerally'. And now, pattern recognition time! What comes next after 霹 thunder and 靂 lightning? Obvious: 霧 fog. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「どうした、二人とも黙っちゃって？　もしかして二人とも、照れちゃってるのか？　おいおい霧はともかく太一、こんな山猿に照れる必要ねーって」
adjudicated.en: Shinkawa: "What's it, you guys just shut up? Don'tcha tell me, you guys're all shy? C'mon, c'mon, I understand Kiri, but Taichi, no need to be all shy in front of this bumpkin, right!"
adjudicated.assessment: Shinkawa says that Kiri may be shy, but Taichi need not be shy around this mountain bumpkin. The English's 'I understand Kiri' changes the concession into comprehension and leaves the bumpkin's referent unclear.

highlights.text: Shinkawa: "What's it, you guys just shut up? Don'tcha tell me, you guys're all shy? C'mon, c'mon, I understand Kiri, but Taichi, no need to be all shy in front of this bumpkin, right!"

adjudicated.jp: 「豊、うるさい……」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "Yutaka, shut up..."
comments: What respect Kiri has for Yutaka. Of course, she's tsundere, but... see CCA0018B -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「……佐倉霧、です」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...I am Sakura Kiri."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「く、黒須太一です」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "I-, I am Kurosu Taichi."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ぎこちなく頭を下げる。
adjudicated.en: I bow my head in awkward embarrassment.
comments: He's more terrified of her than she is of him. Oh, it's an act, of course... see CCC3027. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「お、お噂はかねがね」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "He-, heard quite a lot about you."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...huh."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: あの戦慄の踵使い……だったのだ。
adjudicated.en: It was her... that terrifying heel user.
comments: Contrast CCC3002. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 確か復讐を誓って別れた。
adjudicated.en: We certainly parted with vows of revenge.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 霧の目に、好意のかけらさえ、まったく見受けられない。
adjudicated.en: I could not catch a glint of favoritism in Kiri's eyes.
comments: That's the word generally used for Youko's feelings for Taichi. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 好意 means goodwill, affection, or favor toward Taichi. 'Favoritism' means unfair preferential treatment and changes the interpersonal judgment.

adjudicated.jp: というか、ジト目である。
adjudicated.en: Or should I say, she's staring at me scornfully.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「こちらもいろいろと噂、聞いてます」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "I have also heard a lot about you, heard indeed."
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says that she too has heard various rumors. The repeated emphatic tag is invented.

adjudicated.jp: 「そ、そう？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Ha-, have you?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 俺は緊張しつつ、ティーカップを口につけた。
adjudicated.en: I put the teacup to my mouth despite the mental strain.
comments: He's a multiple murderer who'd take three seconds to crush her if he ever got serious, and the only competition in there's a cripple. Why would he have a mental strain? At least part of this must be pretension. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「いやー、この紅茶、甘いなー！　まるで砂糖みたい、うん。それになんだかざらざらするね。新食感ってやつか」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Wooow, this black tea's sweet ain't iiit! It's just like sugar, yes. And somehow just a little coarse and granular. It's a novel food texture ain't it."
comments: He just gulped down a teacup with nothing but sugar in it, didn't he. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source is strained comic small talk but does not supply specifically British negative tags.
The source text has multiple authoritative occurrences and this unit lacks a unique binding.

adjudicated.jp: きつい。
adjudicated.en: Harsh.
comments: See CCA0015
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ことほどさようにツッコミとは、ある意味慈愛でもあるのだ。
adjudicated.en: The performance of a Straight-Man Retort is, in a certain sense, a representation of reciprocal kindness.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says that tsukkomi is in one sense an act of benevolence. The English invents capitalization and 'reciprocal,' while its cumbersome gloss describes a performed representation rather than the retort itself.

highlights.text: a Straight-Man Retort is, in a certain sense, a representation of reciprocal kindness

adjudicated.jp: 「つうか、ナチュラルに砂糖じゃん、それ」
adjudicated.en: Shinkawa: "Right, naturally, ain't it sugar that."
comments: Seems he spotted him drinking a cup of sugar. Pun is "it's natural sugar" + "of course, moron, that's just sugar". -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says, 'That's literally just sugar.' The English forms neither a grammatical question nor declaration.

adjudicated.jp: 「……いたみいる」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...I am greatly obliged."
comments: For the tsukkomi. Even if it's sub-Tomoki level. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 身に染みた。
adjudicated.en: It's something that went all the way down to the heart.
comments: See CCC3027 - black sugar sediments in the heart... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 身に染みた means that the remark hit home or sank in. The English literalizes a physical path and uses 'to' rather than an idiomatic emotional construction.

highlights.text: went all the way down to the heart

adjudicated.jp: 「……なんでも、手当たり次第にセクハラをしてらっしゃるとか」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...I am told that you perform sexual harassment on anyone and everyone you can lay your hands on."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「そーなんだよコイツ、やることすげーの。かなりびびるよ」
adjudicated.en: Shinkawa: "Doooes 'e now, this guy, that's some weeeird stuff he does. Pretty freaky!"
adjudicated.assessment: Shinkawa agrees that this is what Taichi does and says his behavior is extreme. The English turns the opening into a malformed question and leaves two competing subjects in one clause.

highlights.text: Doooes 'e now, this guy, that's some weeeird stuff he does.

adjudicated.jp: 「ああ、いや、それはね、セクハラといいますか……その……性的愛情表現って感じで決してやましい意図ではないという」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, no, that would be well, calling it something like sexual harassment... it is... a sexual related expression of endearment that has no guilty intent whatsoever!"
comments: I think he meant "mean intent" there, but... cross conversation! -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese calls it a sexual expression of affection. The English uses the noun 'sexual' where the compound requires 'sexually related' or a direct adjective.

highlights.text: a sexual related expression of endearment

adjudicated.jp: 「そういうの、セクハラって言います」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "And that is called, 'sexual harassment'."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「あー、そうだったけかな！　ハハハ……」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, that is what it seemed like! HA. HA. HA..."
comments: Mechanical laugh + continuing cross conversations. While the metasuggestions are that this his awkwarndness is real, from Kiri's side, Taichi is being a dangerous sociopath. That's why Kiri hates his guts. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: そうだったっけ asks whether that was what the behavior was called. The English instead says the classification merely seemed that way.

highlights.text: that is what it seemed like

adjudicated.jp: 見えないナイフが、ざくざく突き刺さってくる。
adjudicated.en: A knife I could not see pierced me with slashes and thrusts.
comments: PCP CCC0014
Origins of the Knife (tune in tonight for part one, only on The History Channel). -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese imagines multiple invisible knives stabbing into him again and again. The English reduces them to one knife and adds slashing as a separate action.

highlights.text: A knife I could not see pierced me with slashes and thrusts.

adjudicated.jp: 「……嫌がってる子も、いますよね？」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...but you do it to the reluctant ones as well, do you?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「あー、嫌がる相手にはちゃんと慎んでるよ？　その、心の底から嫌がる相手は、わかるんで、ハイ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, I'm properly prudent with reluctant partners you know? That is, I can tell when a partner is disagreeing from the bottom of the heart, yesss!"
comments: Ambiguity continues -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Taichi says he properly refrains with anyone who truly dislikes it. The English substitutes being 'prudent,' calls the girls partners, and weakens deep aversion to merely disagreeing.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ahhh, I'm properly prudent with reluctant partners you know? That is, I can tell when a partner is disagreeing from the bottom of the heart, yesss!"

adjudicated.jp: 「じゃあ、みゆきはセクハラを望んでいるんですか？」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "Did Miyuki wish to be sexually harassed then?"
comments: Did you see the goalpost move? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「あー、まあ嫌がってる、かな？　けどそれは表面的でしてな、お嬢さん。ホレ、口ではなんといっても体は正直みたいな」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, was she reluctant, maybe I wonder? But that's just on the surface it is, ojou-san. Yes, because even if her mouth doesn't say it, her body has evidence."
comments: See CCA0012. Recurring ain't it. Right now, the reader should be thinking that he wasn't being funny when he wrote that, which is why it was repeated right at the start of this route. Kiri certainly doesn't. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Taichi claims her reluctance is only superficial and invokes the cliche that whatever the mouth says, the body is honest. The English shifts to past tense and changes bodily honesty into unspecified 'evidence.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ahhh, was she reluctant, maybe I wonder? But that's just on the surface it is, ojou-san. Yes, because even if her mouth doesn't say it, her body has evidence."

adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...disgusting."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 吐き捨てるような小声。
adjudicated.en: In a low voice, as if spitting my way.
comments: See parts of Week 1... right around before meeting Kiri, actually. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Kiri speaks in a low voice as though spitting the words out. The English makes the narrator the object of spitting and uses 'way' without a meaningful role.

adjudicated.jp: 俺には聞こえた。
adjudicated.en: I heard it, but,
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: バームクーヘンの縞模様を薄くはがすことに熱中している豊には、聞こえない。
adjudicated.en: Yutaka did not hear, lost as he is his enthusiastic tearing apart a Baumkuchen by thin stripes.
comments: great now I'm hungry again. This way of eating it seems to be the subject of at least one moe slice of life scene. I wouldn't know since I'm a teh litfags or something so I don't watch Animuhs unless they have like 300000 Hard Kanji's per scene or stuff. More on the topic: does Yutaka have ears that know how to hear? This is important, see Sakuraba below. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Yutaka is absorbed in peeling apart the cake's thin striped layers. The English omits 'in' after 'lost,' makes enthusiasm possess the action, and changes layers into a method 'by stripes.'

highlights.text: lost as he is his enthusiastic tearing apart a Baumkuchen by thin stripes

adjudicated.jp: このガキ、空気を読むということをしないのか。
adjudicated.en: Can't this ghoul of a brat just not read the mood?
comments: Another absolutely normal term that is also the name of a traditional Japanese monster, see CCA0018B. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Taichi asks whether the brat cannot read the room. The English adds 'ghoul' and its double negative instead asks whether he can refrain from reading it.

highlights.text: Can't this ghoul of a brat just not read the mood?

adjudicated.jp: アイサインをばちばち送る。
adjudicated.en: Crackle, crackle an electric eye-sign is sent.
comments: See CCC0026 -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Shinkawa: "!"
comments: This used the wrong nametag, fixed in the console version. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 豊が気づく。
adjudicated.en: Yutaka notices.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: そうだよ、助けてくれ！
adjudicated.en: Yes, help me please!
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 俺は目で雄弁に語った。
adjudicated.en: I speak with eloquence via eyes.
comments: See CCA0027, CCB0022 -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says Taichi speaks eloquently with his eyes. English requires a determiner or possessive before the plural body part.

adjudicated.en: Shinkawa: "!!!"
comments: Idem. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 豊は部長クラスの誇らしげな顔で、任せておけとばかりに小さく頷く。
adjudicated.en: With a face that's Club President Class as far as pride, Yutaka signaled a "leave it all to me!" with a tiny nod.
comments: I think this means his disattention is Misato class, i.e. he's wilfully disregarding what's going on. All he's reading is that Taichi likes Kiri; unfortunately, he isn't wrong in the slightest. Like Sakuraba, he tends to react to what Taichi means, not to what he says. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「あ……やべ、生理はじまった。俺、ナプキン買ってくるから、その間二人で話しててくれよな？」
adjudicated.en: Shinkawa: "Ah... no way, my period's begun. I gotta put on a pad, so in the while you two get chatting will you?"
comments: As far as bad lies, this is Taichi level. Of course, they have the same backstory, likely the same teacher(s). However, what you're now wondering if whether Shinkawa, due to his backstory, has regular blood leaks from his being repeate-GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Shinkawa's excuse says he will go buy pads and asks them to talk in the meantime. The English changes buying to wearing one and uses the malformed temporal phrase 'in the while.'

highlights.text: I gotta put on a pad, so in the while

adjudicated.en: Shinkawa: "?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 何も理解していなかった。
adjudicated.en: He didn't understand anything at all.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 二人きりになったら、気まずさの爆弾が炸裂しそうだ。
adjudicated.en: This bomb of unpleasantness might just explode if it's just the two of us alone.
comments: The explosive birth of the Humanity Annihilation Bomb? Also, futari-KIRI. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「わたしには、みゆきがスカートをめくられたがってる……とは思えないです」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "Miyuki wanted her skirt flipped you say... that did not appear to be the case to me."
adjudicated.assessment: Kiri says she cannot believe Miyuki wants the treatment. The English changes the present desire under discussion into a completed past desire.

adjudicated.jp: 「んー、そ、そう？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Mmmh, re-, really?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 豊は再び、バームクーヘンを解体しはじめる。
adjudicated.en: Yutaka begins once more his disassembly of the Baumkuchen.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: アカン……この人……。
adjudicated.en: Hopeless... this guy is just...
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「だから黒須先輩のしてることは、どうかと思います」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "Therefore, what you have done, Kurosu-senpai, is something I have a problem with."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ハッキリ言う。
adjudicated.en: So she says sharply.
comments: HakKIRI. Damn puns... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 冷静に見ると、嫌いなタイプじゃない。
adjudicated.en: Looked at calmly, she is not the disliking type.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says that, viewed calmly, Kiri is not a type Taichi dislikes. The English instead says that Kiri herself is not prone to disliking others.

highlights.text: she is not the disliking type

adjudicated.jp: むしろ好ましい……近づきたいと思わせる少女だった。
adjudicated.en: Rather, the likeable one... a girl that leaves me the sense of a desire to approach.
comments: Also be a measure of what she is (dere with a cover of tsun due to circumstances, like Touko), not just that she's his type... if only because his type is "attractive human females". ...well, "attractive aloof females", but... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says she is actually likable, a girl who makes him want to get closer. The English lacks the subject for 'the likeable one' and converts desire into a sense she leaves him.

highlights.text: the likeable one... a girl that leaves me the sense of a desire to approach

adjudicated.jp: 少し気が抜けた。
adjudicated.en: I felt a bit relaxed.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ちゃんと話したくなった。
adjudicated.en: I wanted to talk frankly to her.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「……佐倉さんは、正義漢だな」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...Sakura-san, you're a woman among women, a Woman of Justice."
comments: 漢. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 正義漢 calls her a person with a strong sense of justice. The English invents a gendered superlative and a capitalized title.

highlights.text: a woman among women, a Woman of Justice

adjudicated.jp: むっとしたようだった。
adjudicated.en: She seemed to grow testy.
comments: Of course, she probably knows this Ally of Justice stuff is just shonen manga crap. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「それがなにか？」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "What would that even be?"
adjudicated.assessment: それがなにか means 'And what of it?' The English instead asks him to identify what the quality is.

adjudicated.jp: 「いや、いいんだ。そういう人間は、どこにだって必要だと思うし」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Welll, it's a good thing. I think that's the kind of human that's necessary anywhere and everywhere."
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says people like that are needed everywhere. The English uses a categorical 'kind of human' and redundantly stacks two universal location phrases.

highlights.text: the kind of human that's necessary anywhere and everywhere

adjudicated.jp: 「……おっしゃる意味がわかりません」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...I do not understand the meaning of your words."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「馬鹿にしてるんじゃないよ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "I'm not ridiculing you here!"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「今まで、キミみたいなタイプ、俺のそばにいなかったからさ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Just, up until now, there's never been your kind of type around me."
comments: This only also refers to tsunderes. Only 'also'. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says he has never had her type around him. 'Kind of type' redundantly combines two classifiers.

adjudicated.jp: 「……そうですか」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...so you say."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 見たら豊は座ったまま寝ていた。
adjudicated.en: Looking over, Yutaka had fallen asleep while still sitting.
comments: Juuust as the conversation turns somewhat serious, Yutaka falls asleep. Were Taichi to have this convenient 'off' switch as well it'd serve as a quick explanation for most of the weirdness here, especially if he can also keep his body moving sort of automatically while he has his flashbacks. Now see CCC3009, CCD1001. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: さすがマイフレン。大物である。
adjudicated.en: Just what I expected, my friend. A VIP you are.
adjudicated.assessment: 大物 calls Yutaka a formidable, unflappable character. 'VIP' instead assigns social importance, and the inversion adds an unsupported voice.

adjudicated.jp: おかげで少しつっこんだ話ができそうだ。
adjudicated.en: And because of that, it seems we can now talk a little more in depth.
comments: Now he wants him gone... but then again, Yutaka can read him correctly, so he could've just done the right thing both times. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「群青はどう？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "How's Gunjou?"
adjudicated.assessment: The standard Hepburn romanization of 群青 is Gunjō, not 'Gunjou.'

adjudicated.jp: 「……どうといいますと？」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...'how' in what sense?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「クラスに編入されてさ、いろんなタイプのヤツがいる。言葉の通じないヤツ、周囲が目に入らないヤツ、突発的に暴れるヤツ、まったく普通人みたいなヤツ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "There's all sorts of types that get put into classes. The type who can't understand your language, the type who doesn't see what's around them, the type that fires into rage suddenly, and the damnably normal-ish types."
comments: Misato and Miki are the first, Taichi is the second, Touko and Kiri are the third, Sakuraba and Tomoki are the fourth. Where Youko fits? Well, it should be obvious: the second. In other words, she's like Taichi. So very much that. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The list describes people one cannot communicate with, people oblivious to their surroundings, people with sudden violent outbursts, and apparently ordinary people. The English narrows communication to 'your language,' literalizes perception, and adds 'damnably.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "There's all sorts of types that get put into classes. The type who can't understand your language, the type who doesn't see what's around them, the type that fires into rage suddenly, and the damnably normal-ish types."

adjudicated.jp: 「けどみんな、世間に適応できなくて弾かれたのばっかりだ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "But all, to the last, have been repelled by society for being unable to conform to it."
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says they were rejected or excluded because they could not adapt to society. 'Repelled' depicts a physical force or mutual disgust rather than social exclusion.

adjudicated.jp: 「みんな、日本で屈指のどうかしてる人間なんだ。もちろん、俺もキミもだよ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Everybody there's one of Japan's foremost damaged humans. Of course, me and you too."
adjudicated.assessment: Taichi calls everyone there one of Japan's most seriously messed-up people, himself and Kiri included. The English lacks a verb, dehumanizes them as 'damaged humans,' and uses object pronouns as subjects.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Everybody there's one of Japan's foremost damaged humans. Of course, me and you too."

adjudicated.en: Kiri: "..."
adjudicated.assessment: The source text has multiple authoritative occurrences and this unit lacks a unique binding.

adjudicated.jp: 「会話できる人間が何人いる？　友達と呼べる関係を築ける相手が何人いた？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "How many humans there that can manage a conversation? How many that can be party to building something that can be called friendship?"
comments: This "human" was censored in the PS2 version, furthering the idea that it should be left literal as often as possible. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese asks how many people can hold a conversation and with how many one can build a relationship called friendship. The first English question lacks 'are,' and the second turns a potential friend into a party to constructing an abstract thing.

highlights.text: Taichi: "How many humans there that can manage a conversation? How many that can be party to building something that can be called friendship?"

adjudicated.jp: 「仮に会話が成立しても、そいつがどんなはずみで暴走するかわからない。不安はいつもつきまとう」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Even if we were to say that a conversation was established, you couldn't even begin to guess what spur would make them explode. Anxiety is always on your heels."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「たとえば……ガラスの割れる音を聞くと、異常に攻撃的になるヤツとかさ。うちのクラスにいるんだけど」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "For example... someone who, when he hears the sound of glass being shattered, starts being abnormally aggressive. He's right in my class, you know."
comments: See CCC0011B, CCC0014. Glasswork gets cracked and he grows aggressive, hum, yes he's in Taichi's class indeed. Don't ask him whether Karade is a ripoff of Karate, either. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says the person becomes abnormally aggressive. 'Starts being' is a clumsy progressive calque for the change of state.

adjudicated.jp: 「さっきの話と、どう関係があるんです？」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "How is this related to what we were discussing earlier?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「キミは俺に正義を説いた」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "You preached justice to me."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「……道理をわきまえた相手として、俺を見ている」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...you see me as someone who can tell right from wrong, who is reasonable."
comments: Overliteralized due to how if you still don't get it I don't know what to do really. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 小ぶりの眉根が寄った。
adjudicated.en: The tiny gap between her eyebrows grew tighter.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says that her small brows draw together. The English makes the gap between them the body part that tightens.

highlights.text: The tiny gap between her eyebrows grew tighter.

adjudicated.jp: 「そういう意味では……」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "But I did not mean..."
adjudicated.assessment: そういう意味では begins a hesitant concession, 'In that sense...' The English instead explicitly denies that she meant it.

adjudicated.jp: 「そういう意味でしょ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "You meant exactly that."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「俺の行動をどうかと思う。そう指摘して弾劾する。直してもらわなければならないと思う」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "You have a problem with my conduct. You point it out and denounce it. It is absolutely unthinkable for you not to come and fix me."
adjudicated.assessment: Taichi says she believes he must correct his conduct. The English makes Kiri personally come fix him and frames failure to do so as unthinkable.

highlights.text: It is absolutely unthinkable for you not to come and fix me.

adjudicated.jp: 「群青でふりかざす考え方じゃないなぁ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "That ain't a way of thinking you can bandy around at Gunjou ya know."
comments: IOW this is her Ultramarine. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Taichi says this is not a principle one should brandish at Gunjō. 'Bandy around' changes aggressive moral wielding into casual circulation, 'Gunjou' is non-Hepburn, and the eye dialect is unsupported.

highlights.text: Taichi: "That ain't a way of thinking you can bandy around at Gunjou ya know."

adjudicated.jp: 「キミがただの鈍い子なのか、それとも逆に、鋭く俺の性根を見抜いているのかはわからない」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Whether you're just dumb, or conversely, you very sharply saw through my character I can't tell."
comments: Choice of training spot, hypocrisy, being exploited by Miki, and being in love with Taichi and expressing it like this. Touko's nowhere near as dumb as her. In fact, the only one dumber than her are possibly Taichi and, by extension, Youko. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 鈍い means obtuse or insensitive here, not simply unintelligent. The English shifts the alternative insight into past tense and fails to close the embedded whether construction before the main clause.

highlights.text: Whether you're just dumb, or conversely, you very sharply saw through my character I can't tell.

adjudicated.jp: 「けど……久しぶりに、新しい出会いの中で人間扱いされた気がした」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "But... it felt like a long time since I've been treated like a human by someone I just met."
comments: ...and yet, by implicitly believing he can improve, despite her Stereotypical Doomsaying Priest attitude, she still understands a little bit of him better than he does. To be able to understand this is the point of the the CS Lewis quote I open the book with. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says it felt like he had been treated as human for the first time in a long while. The English instead makes the elapsed time itself the feeling and mixes past and present perfect.

highlights.text: it felt like a long time since I've been treated

adjudicated.assessment: The source text has multiple authoritative occurrences and this unit lacks a unique binding.

adjudicated.en: She opens her mouth, agape.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 気を抜くと、なるほど歳相応に可愛らしい。
adjudicated.en: When she loses focus a bit, she has the cuteness suitable for a girl her age.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 豊の目は節穴だな。
adjudicated.en: Yutaka's eyes are knotholes indeed.
adjudicated.assessment: 目は節穴 is an idiom meaning that Yutaka is a poor judge or effectively blind to her appeal. The English exposes the literal knotholes without conveying that function.

adjudicated.jp: 「……そーいう話をしているのではなく！」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...that isn't what we are talking about!"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「みゆきは」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Miyuki, she..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 激昂が凍りつく。
adjudicated.en: Her indignation freezes.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「あれで結構、重いんだ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "She was quite serious... in that regard."
adjudicated.assessment: 重い here means that Miyuki's condition is fairly severe. 'Serious in that regard' is vague and can instead describe her attitude.

adjudicated.jp: 「詳しくは知らないけど、本人が孤独を感じすぎると、発症するみたい」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "I don't know the details, but, it seems that when she starts feeling excessively lonely her symptoms come out."
adjudicated.assessment: 発症する means that the condition manifests or she has an episode. Symptoms do not idiomatically 'come out' in English.

adjudicated.jp: 「外界失認ってやつだ。世界の輪郭があいまいになる。一種のトリップだな。もっとも屋上から落ちやすいタイプ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "She has External World Agnosia. The outline of the world becomes fuzzy and unclear. Kind of a drug trip. She's the type that'd fall from the rooftop easily."
comments: http://www.britannica.com/EBchecked/topic/9353/agnosia See CCA0016. This is exactly what Taichi has. The part about the rooftop is particularly ironic given Yutaka. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「知ってた？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Did you know?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...no."
adjudicated.assessment: The source text has multiple authoritative occurrences and this unit lacks a unique binding.

adjudicated.jp: 「たぶんあの子は、移動になっちゃうと思うよ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "I think that she'll end up transferred, maybe."
comments: Interesting uncertainty. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「え……移動というのは……？」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "Eh... what do you mean, transferred...?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「ちゃんとした病院施設に送られるってこと」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "That she'll be sent to a proper hospitalization facility."
comments: This is the only indication that Class X isn't just another classroom. Then again, there's no certainty that Taichi knows, at this point, where she'll be transferred exactly, or even what Class X entails. It could even be "the" Research Building of CCA0013. This may be a plot hole, intentional deception, plot relevant or simply the character hazarding a guess with pretty much equal probability. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says she will be sent to a proper hospital facility. 'Hospitalization facility' is a nonstandard tautological compound.

adjudicated.jp: 「それって……」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "But that's..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 霧は絶句したようだった。
adjudicated.en: Kiri appeared speechless.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「ホラ、学校だとどうしても孤独な時間ってあるだろ？　周囲が全員健常者なら気づかってあげられるけどさ……みんな自分のことで精一杯だし」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Come now, it's a school, aren't there hours where we're alone as a matter of course? If all around us there were healthy people they'd worry about it but... everyone's just doing what they can about themselves."
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says that if everyone around her were healthy, they could look out for her. The English changes active care for a person into worrying about an unspecified situation.

adjudicated.jp: 「みゆきのもっとも嫌う、孤独な時ってのが、どこにでもある」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Those hours of solitude, what Miyuki hated most, they're everywhere."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: たとえば放課後。誰もいない教室。
adjudicated.en: For example, after school. A classroom with no one inside.
comments: Also see CCA0015C. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: たとえば校庭。無人のトラック。
adjudicated.en: For example, the courtyard. The sports track left depopulated.
comments: See CCA0007. For example, the interior of the broadcast room. In which she was sealed despite Tomoki being right nearby for no apparent reason. Very likely, her condition is similar to present Taichi's: she just daydreams a lot. Later on, however... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 無人 means simply empty or unoccupied. 'Depopulated' implies an established population was removed.

adjudicated.jp: たとえば教室。人がいても人同士の接続がない、断絶空間。
adjudicated.en: For example, the classroom. There are people, but no one to have a connection or a fellowship with; it is a space of disintegration.
comments: Do you feel it, beating over your head yet? How about now? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese describes a room where people are present but disconnected from one another, a space of severance. The English instead says there is no available person to connect with and calls the space one of disintegration.

highlights.text: For example, the classroom. There are people, but no one to have a connection or a fellowship with; it is a space of disintegration.

adjudicated.jp: 「どこにだって空白はあるのさ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Wherever you go there are vacuums, you know."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「彼女が放送部に入ってるのは、ウチが自意識を保持している連中の集団だからだ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "She had joined the Broadcast Club because this in-group was an assembly of people maintaining a sense of self."
adjudicated.assessment: ウチ means their club, not a sociological in-group. The English also shifts the continuing reason for her membership into past tense and uses an abstract 'assembly.'

adjudicated.jp: 「そういう意図のもとで放送部は成立してる」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "The Broadcast Club had been established with that intention as foundation."
comments: Now this is odd. Was this official? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The club exists on the basis of that intention. The English uses past perfect for an ongoing institution and omits the determiner before 'foundation.'

highlights.text: had been established with that intention as foundation

adjudicated.jp: 「他に部活なんていくつもないからね」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "'Cause there's not much activity in the club besides that, you know."
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says there are not many other clubs. The English instead says this club contains little activity beyond the stated purpose.

highlights.text: there's not much activity in the club besides that

adjudicated.jp: 肩をすくめた。
adjudicated.en: I shrugged my shoulders.
comments: PCP CCC0014
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「友達を作るのは大変だ。でも作らずにはいられない。どうしてかわかる？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Making friends is a hassle. But going without making some is unacceptable. Do you know why?"
adjudicated.assessment: 大変 means difficult, not merely bothersome. 作らずにはいられない says people cannot help making friends, whereas the English turns that compulsion into a normative prohibition.

highlights.text: going without making some is unacceptable

adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...no."
adjudicated.assessment: The source text has multiple authoritative occurrences and this unit lacks a unique binding.

adjudicated.assessment: 心を育てる means nurturing emotional or mental development. 'Rearing' ordinarily applies to children or animals and treats a heart as an independent creature.
